question: On 14 February 2024, the Commission published two documents pertaining to the monitoring of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 on the dissemination of terrorist content online: the implementation report, wherein the Commission asserts that the regulation is meeting its objectives effectively and a Commission staff working paper outlining a comprehensive monitoring programme designed to evaluate the outputs, results, and impacts of the regulation, with the intention of producing an evaluation report, scheduled for 7 June 2024.
Considering the deliberate removal of referrals from the regulation due to potential legal ambiguity and adverse effects on fundamental rights, why has the Commission emphasised their convenience?
When can Parliament expect the publication of the evaluation report and what factors are causing the deviation from the originally planned timeline?

Can the Commission elaborate on why it believes that the indicators outlined in the detailed monitoring programme are sufficient to genuinely ensure the proper safeguarding of fundamental rights, especially considering that service providers will want to self-report diligence and the consideration of rights?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.7.2024) Regulation 2021/784 requires that the Member States’ competent authorities have the power to send removal orders requiring hosting service providers to remove terrorist content or to disable access thereto in all Member States.

Recital 40 of Regulation 2021/784 states that referrals by Member States and Europol have proven to be an effective and swift means of increasing hosting service providers’ awareness of specific content available through their services, that such referrals should remain available in addition to removal orders and that nothing in the Regulation should be understood as precluding the use of referrals.

The adoption of the evaluation report is foreseen for the second quarter of 20251. The evaluation report will follow up to the adoption of the implementation and the monitoring programme, which was delayed due to the late transmission to the Commission of key information from Member States and hosting service providers.

It was also considered important to reflect the application of the Regulation following the terrorist attack perpetrated by Hamas against Israel on 7 October 2023. The monitoring programme aims at collecting information to support the evaluation of the Regulation pursuant to Article 23 including the impact on fundamental rights.

The monitoring programme includes a wide set of indicators under which data will be collected from competent authorities and hosting service providers. Result indicators will seek to measure the functioning and effectiveness of the safeguard mechanisms once they have been implemented and impacts indicators will help measure the long-term impact of the Regulation on specific areas like fundamental rights.
